definitions.gloss: cram school; tutoring school; after-school study school
definitions.explanation: A private supplementary school where students attend after regular school hours to prepare for entrance exams or improve academic performance. A central part of the Japanese education system.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}に{通|かよ}わせている。
examples.english: I'm sending my child to a cram school.

examples.japanese: {学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}の{月謝|げっしゃ}は{結構|けっこう}{高|たか}い。
examples.english: The monthly tuition for cram school is quite expensive.

examples.japanese: {中学|ちゅうがく}{受験|じゅけん}のために、{小学|しょうがく}4{年生|ねんせい}から{学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}に{通|かよ}い{始|はじ}める{子|こ}どもが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many children start attending cram school from the fourth grade of elementary school in preparation for middle school entrance exams.

notes:
Composed of {学習|がくしゅう} (study, learning) + {塾|じゅく} (private school). This is the formal term for cram schools; in everyday conversation, people often say simply {塾|じゅく}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}に{通|かよ}う: to attend a cram school
- {学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}の{講師|こうし}: cram school instructor
- {学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}の{月謝|げっしゃ}: cram school monthly tuition
- {個別|こべつ}{指導|しどう}{塾|じゅく}: individual tutoring school

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {塾|じゅく}: cram school — shorter, more casual version of the same concept
- {予備校|よびこう}: prep school — specifically for university entrance exam preparation, typically for high school students
- {進学塾|しんがくじゅく}: advancement-oriented cram school — focused specifically on entrance exam preparation

CULTURAL NOTE:
Cram schools are a major part of Japanese education culture. According to surveys, over half of Japanese middle school students attend some form of {塾|じゅく}. The industry is large, with major chains like {河合塾|かわいじゅく} and {日能研|にちのうけん} being household names.
